title: Stack-Overflow-like Q&A
scopeHtml:
Scope: questions, answers, votes with delta reputation, accept, tag index, per-post locking.

Scope: questions, answers, votes with delta reputation, accept, tag index, per-post locking.

notes.title: Requirements
notes.html:
Design a Stack-Overflow-like Q&A site: users ask questions with tags, post answers, vote, the asker accepts one answer, and reputation changes accordingly.

Clarify:

  • Functional: ask, answer, upvote/downvote (one vote per user per post, changeable), accept answer, search by title word, browse by tag.
  • Rules: no self-voting; only the asker accepts; accepting a new answer moves the badge.
  • Out of scope: comments, bounties, moderation, full-text ranking.
  • Scale talk: Stack Overflow famously served huge traffic from a few SQL Server machines because the workload is read-heavy; the LLD interest is the vote and reputation rules.

Worked example. ben answers; cy upvotes: ben +10. asha accepts: ben +15 (rep 25). cy flips the vote to a downvote: score goes from +1 to -1 (delta of -2) and ben loses 2 x 5 = 10 (rep 15). Flipping must change the vote, not add a second one.

Industry examples. Stack Overflow gives +10 for an answer upvote, +5 for a question upvote, +15 for an accepted answer (confirm current values on their help pages). Reddit and Quora keep a similar vote ledger per user per post.

Everyday analogy. A show of hands where each person has one hand and may lower and raise it again.

Common interview traps.

  • Counting votes as a plain integer, so one user can vote many times.
  • Forgetting to reverse reputation when a vote changes.

notes.title: Core entities
notes.html:
• User (name, reputation).
  • Post abstract base: author, body, score, votes map (voter to +1/-1).
  • Question extends Post: title, tags, answers, accepted answer.
  • Answer extends Post: accepted flag.
  • Forum: all questions, tag index, search.

Decision gravity. Votes are stored as a per-post Map<User, Integer>, not as a counter. That is the only way to support "change my vote" and "remove my vote". Reversible: in memory yes; once persisted, the votes table (post, user, value) with a unique key is a one-way door but the right one.

Everyday analogy. An attendance sheet with names, not a tally on a whiteboard.

Common interview traps.

  • Two near-identical classes for question and answer voting.
  • Reputation derived on the fly versus stored: say which and why (stored is fast, derived is auditable).

notes.title: Class diagram
notes.html:
+---------------------+
              | <<abstract>> Post   |
              | author body score   |
              | votes: Map<User,int>|
              | vote(user, dir)     |
              | upRep()  (abstract) |
              +---------------------+
                 ^                ^
        +-----------------+   +-----------+
        | Question        |1-*| Answer    |
        | title tags      |-->| accepted  |
        | accepted        |   | upRep()=10|
        | accept()        |   +-----------+
        | upRep()=5       |
        +-----------------+
Forum: questions, tagIndex  -> ask(), byTag(), search()
User: reputation

Common interview traps.

  • Putting reputation math in the Forum instead of next to the vote.

notes.title: Key patterns
notes.html:
• Template method: Post.vote holds the shared algorithm; subclasses override upRep(). Alternative: a ReputationPolicy strategy, better if rules become configurable. Reversible: yes.
  • Inverted index for tags: Map<tag, List<Question>> makes byTag O(1) lookup instead of scanning all questions.
  • Delta-based update in vote: compute delta = new - old and apply once. This single idea handles new vote, flip, and (with 0) retract.
  • Not used: Observer for reputation, until badges or notifications are asked for.

Worked example. Old vote +1, new -1: delta -2, score drops by 2, author loses 2 * (upRep/2) = 10 for an answer. New vote from nothing, +1: delta +1.

Industry examples. Stack Overflow also caps daily reputation gain and reverses it when a post is deleted; Reddit fuzzes displayed scores to resist vote manipulation.

Everyday analogy. Updating your restaurant review: the average adjusts by the difference, not by adding a second review.

Common interview traps.

  • Using separate branches for "first vote" and "flip" and getting one wrong.
  • Integer division surprises in the downvote penalty; state your rule.

notes.title: Code
notes.html:
import java.util.*;

class User { final String name; int reputation; User(String n) { name = n; } }

abstract class Post {
    final User author; final String body; int score;
    final Map<User, Integer> votes = new HashMap<>();   // one vote per user
    Post(User a, String b) { author = a; body = b; }
    abstract int upRep();                                // reputation per upvote
    void vote(User voter, int dir) {                     // dir = +1 or -1
        if (voter == author) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no self vote");
        Integer old = votes.put(voter, dir);
        int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
        score += delta;
        author.reputation += delta * (delta > 0 ? upRep() : upRep() / 2);
    }
}
class Answer extends Post {
    boolean accepted;
    Answer(User a, String b) { super(a, b); }
    int upRep() { return 10; }
}
class Question extends Post {
    final String title; final Set<String> tags; final List<Answer> answers = new ArrayList<>();
    Answer accepted;
    Question(User a, String t, String b, Set<String> tags) { super(a, b); title = t; this.tags = tags; }
    int upRep() { return 5; }
    Answer answer(User u, String body) { Answer a = new Answer(u, body); answers.add(a); return a; }
    void accept(User asker, Answer a) {
        if (asker != author) throw new SecurityException("only asker accepts");
        if (accepted != null) { accepted.accepted = false; accepted.author.reputation -= 15; }
        accepted = a; a.accepted = true; a.author.reputation += 15;
    }
}

class Forum {
    private final List<Question> questions = new ArrayList<>();
    private final Map<String, List<Question>> tagIndex = new HashMap<>();
    Question ask(User u, String title, String body, String... tags) {
        Question q = new Question(u, title, body, Set.of(tags));
        questions.add(q);
        for (String t : tags) tagIndex.computeIfAbsent(t, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(q);
        return q;
    }
    List<Question> byTag(String t) { return tagIndex.getOrDefault(t, List.of()); }
    List<Question> search(String word) {
        List<Question> r = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Question q : questions) if (q.title.toLowerCase().contains(word.toLowerCase())) r.add(q);
        return r;
    }
}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Forum f = new Forum();
        User asha = new User("asha"), ben = new User("ben"), cy = new User("cy");
        Question q = f.ask(asha, "How does HashMap resize?", "details", "java", "collections");
        Answer a = q.answer(ben, "At load factor 0.75 it doubles.");
        a.vote(cy, +1);
        q.accept(asha, a);
        System.out.println("ben rep " + ben.reputation + " score " + a.score);   // 25, 1
        a.vote(cy, -1);                                                          // flips, not adds
        System.out.println("ben rep " + ben.reputation + " score " + a.score);
        if (a.score != -1) throw new AssertionError();
        System.out.println(f.byTag("java").size() + " " + f.search("hashmap").size());
    }
}

Kotlin core:

class User(val name: String) { var reputation = 0 }

abstract class Post(val author: User, val body: String) {
    var score = 0; private set
    private val votes = mutableMapOf<User, Int>()
    protected abstract val upRep: Int
    fun vote(voter: User, dir: Int) {
        require(voter !== author) { "no self vote" }
        val delta = dir - (votes.put(voter, dir) ?: 0)
        score += delta
        author.reputation += delta * if (delta > 0) upRep else upRep / 2
    }
}

class Answer(author: User, body: String) : Post(author, body) {
    override val upRep = 10
    var accepted = false
}

class Question(author: User, val title: String, body: String, val tags: Set<String>) : Post(author, body) {
    override val upRep = 5
    val answers = mutableListOf<Answer>()
    var accepted: Answer? = null
    fun accept(asker: User, a: Answer) {
        check(asker === author) { "only asker accepts" }
        accepted?.let { it.accepted = false; it.author.reputation -= 15 }
        accepted = a; a.accepted = true; a.author.reputation += 15
    }
}

Common interview traps.

  • Forgetting to un-accept the previous answer.

notes.title: Run and test
notes.html:
javac -d out Main.java
java -cp out Main
ben rep 25 score 1
ben rep 15 score -1
1 1

Test: self-vote rejected, non-asker accept rejected, vote flip, re-accept, tag lookup, case-insensitive search.

Common interview traps.

  • No test for the flip path.

notes.title: Concurrency
notes.html:
Races: two votes from different users interleave score += delta (lost update); the same user double-clicks (two threads both see old == null); accept double-credits.

Thread-safe version. Make the vote operation atomic per post.

abstract class Post {
    private final Map<User, Integer> votes = new HashMap<>();
    private int score;

    synchronized void vote(User voter, int dir) {              // lock per post: votes on different posts run in parallel
        if (voter == author) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no self vote");
        Integer old = votes.put(voter, dir);
        int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
        score += delta;
        author.addReputation(delta * (delta > 0 ? upRep() : upRep() / 2));
    }
    synchronized int score() { return score; }
}

class User {
    private final AtomicInteger reputation = new AtomicInteger();
    void addReputation(int d) { reputation.addAndGet(d); }     // many posts update one author
}

The per-post synchronized makes the same-user double click safe (second call sees the first's vote). Reputation uses an atomic because different posts by the same author update it concurrently. No lock is held across two posts, so there is no deadlock.

Production note (gravity). In SQL: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (post_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value, and the score is updated by a trigger or by a periodic recount. Hot questions (a viral post getting thousands of votes a minute) cause row contention, so large sites batch vote counters through a queue or cache and apply them asynchronously.

Common interview traps.

  • A global lock on the Forum.
  • Using ConcurrentHashMap for votes and thinking the compound read-modify-write is atomic. It is not.

notes.title: Follow-ups
notes.html:
• Comments: a third Post subtype or a separate list; they do not vote the same way.
  • Search ranking: inverted index plus score boost.
  • Reputation privileges (downvote needs 125): a policy check in vote.
  • Edit history and moderation: store revisions.
  • Duplicate close votes and bounties.

Common interview traps.

  • Re-scanning every question for each search request at scale.

notes.title: Summary
notes.html:
• Post base class owns voting; subclasses set reputation values (template method).
  • Store votes per voter; apply delta = new - old once.
  • Tag index gives O(1) tag browsing.
  • Accept moves the badge and reverses old reputation.
  • Concurrency: lock per post, atomic reputation, constraint-based upsert in SQL.

questions.promptHtml: Why does each post store a map of voter to vote instead of just an integer score?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tests whether you derive the data structure from the rules (one vote per user, changeable, retractable).

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: A counter cannot know who already voted, so one user could vote 100 times and nobody could change or remove a vote. The map voter -> +1/-1 is a small ledger: it enforces one vote per user, and lets me compute the delta when a vote changes. In SQL it becomes a table (post_id, user_id, value) with a unique key.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
state              action        old   new   delta  score
no vote            upvote        0     +1    +1     +1
+1                 flip to down  +1    -1    -2     -1
-1                 retract       -1    0     +1     0

The same formula delta = new - old handles first vote, flip and retract. Storing a ledger also makes the score auditable and rebuildable.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
Languages: Java, Kotlin

Languages: Java · Kotlin

int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
score += delta;
val delta = dir - (votes.put(voter, dir) ?: 0)
score += delta

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Plain integer score.
  • Separate code branches for "first vote" and "flip" (one will be wrong).
  • Treating retract as "remove entry" but forgetting to reverse the reputation.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. How do you retract a vote? -> dir = 0 (or remove entry) and apply delta = 0 - old.
  2. Where does the uniqueness live in SQL? -> Unique key (post_id, user_id) plus an upsert.
  3. Stored score vs counting rows on every read? -> Stored is fast but can drift, so a periodic recount verifies it; counting is exact but slow on hot posts.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE says "to prevent double voting". Senior adds the delta formula, the DB constraint, and the stored-versus-derived trade-off.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A feed counted likes with count++ and a duplicate-click bug inflated scores until a unique constraint was added.

questions.subtopic: reputation rules as template method vs strategy
questions.promptHtml: Questions give +5 per upvote, answers +10. How do you model it, and when would you change the model?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Checks pattern choice with a reason, and awareness of when a simple inheritance is outgrown.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: A Post base class owns the shared vote algorithm and calls an abstract upRep() that Question and Answer override: that is the Template Method. If the rules become configurable (per-site values, caps, bonuses, time-based decay), I move to a ReputationPolicy strategy injected into the vote, because inheritance fixes the numbers at compile time.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Template method wins now: two subtypes, two constants, no duplication, the shared algorithm cannot be forgotten. It loses when rules vary by something other than post type (user privilege level, daily cap of 200 rep, rep reversed on deletion).

Post.vote(voter, dir)
   check rules -> delta -> score -> author.rep += delta * rate(upRep)
                                       ^ subclass hook

Both are reversible: the public method stays vote(user, dir).

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Reputation math in Forum, away from the vote.
  • Two near-identical vote methods in Question and Answer.
  • Integer division on downvote penalty (upRep()/2) without stating the rule.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Add a daily cap of 200 rep? -> State per user per day; this belongs in a policy, not in the subclasses.
  2. Downvote costs the voter 1 rep? -> Another effect; a policy returns both effects.
  3. Could Observer help? -> Yes once badges or notifications react to reputation changes; not before.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE says "use inheritance". Senior also says when to stop using it and why the public API need not change.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Rep rules scattered across three services produced users whose rep depended on which endpoint was used.

questions.contextHtml:
A new hire reimplemented vote to "simplify" it. Tests for first upvote pass. QA reports: flipping up to down leaves score +1 instead of -1, and ben's reputation keeps growing as cy toggles.

Languages: Java · Kotlin
void vote(User voter, int dir) {
    if (voter == author) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no self vote");
    votes.put(voter, dir);
    score += dir;
    author.reputation += dir * upRep();
}
fun vote(voter: User, dir: Int) {
    require(voter !== author) { "no self vote" }
    votes[voter] = dir
    score += dir
    author.reputation += dir * upRep
}
questions.promptHtml: Find the bugs, give the corrected version and test cases.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add a check if the user already voted and return" which blocks flipping altogether.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is a downvote worth half an upvote (original rule)? Can a vote be retracted?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Revert to the delta version and recount scores of affected posts.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) the map records the vote but the score ignores the old value, so each change adds instead of replacing; (b) reputation uses dir not delta, so repeated toggles keep paying; (c) downvote penalty not scaled.
  4. How I'd verify each: Test: +1 then -1 must give score -1 (delta -2), and rep back down by 2 x 5.
  5. Root cause: The code stores the new vote but applies it as if it were a brand new vote.
  6. Fix:
Languages: Java · Kotlin
Integer old = votes.put(voter, dir);
int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
score += delta;
author.reputation += delta * (delta > 0 ? upRep() : upRep() / 2);
val delta = dir - (votes.put(voter, dir) ?: 0)
score += delta
author.reputation += delta * if (delta > 0) upRep else upRep / 2
  1. Prevention: Table-driven tests of all transitions (none to up, up to down, down to none, same vote twice -> delta 0). A recount job that compares score with the sum of the ledger.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not special-case "flip" separately. For repeated same vote delta is 0, so it is naturally idempotent.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Same user sends +1 twice? -> delta 0, nothing changes.
  • A flip changes reputation by an odd number due to integer division? -> State the rule (delta * upRep / 2 with rounding) and test it; or keep reputation in half-points.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A ranking bug let users farm points by repeatedly toggling a vote; a nightly recount from the ledger found it.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: blocks changing a vote.
  • Hire: delta formula and flip test.
  • Strong hire: also covers idempotency, odd rounding, and a recount safety net.

questions.contextHtml: Product adds: (1) downvoting requires 125 reputation; (2) a user can earn at most 200 reputation per day from votes; (3) comments (not votable) are added under questions and answers; (4) deleting a post reverses the reputation it earned.
questions.promptHtml: Which classes change, where do the new rules live, and what stays closed to modification?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Adds if (user.reputation < 125) and a daily counter directly into Post.vote and makes Comment extends Post with a no-op vote.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is the 200 cap per calendar day or rolling 24 h? Does accept rep count against the cap? Is reversing a deletion capped too?
  2. Immediate mitigation: N/A; I'd first extract a ReputationPolicy because the rules now vary by user state.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Options: stuff into Post.vote; a policy object consulted by vote; an event-driven reputation service.
  4. How I'd verify each: Which option keeps Question/Answer untouched? The policy one.
  5. Root cause: Rules now depend on the voter (privilege) and author (daily total), not only on post type, so inheritance can no longer hold them.
  6. Fix: Post.vote asks policy.canDownvote(voter) and policy.award(author, points, today). Comment is not a Post subtype with fake voting: make Votable the base and Comment outside it (interface segregation, no empty vote). Deletion reverses by replaying the ledger for that post, so a ledger table is required.
  7. Prevention: Tests at 124 and 125 rep, cap boundary at 199 + 10, deletion reversal restores both author and voters' state.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not subclass Comment extends Post to inherit a method it must throw from (LSP violation).

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Cap resets at midnight in which timezone? -> UTC, and inject the clock for tests.
  • Reputation read speed after adding ledger replays? -> Keep stored reputation, rebuild only on deletion or audit.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A rule that "comments can be upvoted" turned Comment into a Post with half the methods unsupported; every caller needed instanceof checks.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: all rules inline.
  • Hire: policy object and a non-votable Comment.
  • Strong hire: ledger-driven reversal, clock injection, boundary tests.

questions.contextHtml: Forum has 2M questions. byTag("java") returns 300,000. The title search loops over every question lowercasing titles: 450 ms per request at 40 requests/s and CPU is 80% on the web tier. Tag browse is already Map<tag, List<Question>> and is fast, but the "java" list is sorted by nothing and the page needs "top 20 by score".
questions.promptHtml: How do you fix search and tag paging, and what do you tell product about relevance?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add caching" or "use Elasticsearch" with no idea what an inverted index is.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Exact word match or substring? Typo tolerance? Freshness requirement after a new question is posted?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Cache hot queries for 30-60 s and cap concurrency while the index is built.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) O(N) scan per request is the cost: 2M x lowercase compare; (b) toLowerCase allocation on every title per request; (c) sorting 300k per tag page.
  4. How I'd verify each: Profile: CPU time in String.toLowerCase/contains; count of titles scanned per request.
  5. Root cause: No index for words. Tag lookup is O(1) because it is an inverted index; title search needs the same idea.
  6. Fix: Tokenise titles at ask-time into Map<word, Set<questionId>> (lowercased once), intersect posting lists for multi-word queries, rank by score or recency. For "top 20 by score" per tag keep a heap/sorted structure or paginate with a cursor on (score, id).
Languages: Java · Kotlin
Map<String, Set<Long>> index = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
void index(Question q) {
    for (String w : q.title.toLowerCase().split("\\W+"))
        index.computeIfAbsent(w, k -> ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()).add(q.id);
}
val index = ConcurrentHashMap<String, MutableSet<Long>>()
fun index(q: Question) {
    q.title.lowercase().split(Regex("\\W+")).forEach {
        index.computeIfAbsent(it) { ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet() }.add(q.id)
    }
}
  1. Prevention: Load test with 2M rows before launch; budget metric for search p95.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not claim an in-memory index scales forever: at this size move to a search engine or SQL full-text, and accept eventual consistency of seconds.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Title edited? -> Remove old words from the index and add new ones in one atomic step per question.
  • Stop words ("the") with million-entry posting lists? -> Skip them, or intersect smallest-first.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A team cached search results but forgot the cache stampede at expiry; the underlying scan then hit all cores at once.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: cache only.
  • Hire: inverted index, ranking separate.
  • Strong hire: update path, cost of posting lists, and when to leave the JVM for a search engine.

questions.contextHtml:
In production a user's browser sends the same upvote twice within 5 ms (double click, no debounce). Post scores sometimes end at +2 from one voter, and the author's reputation shows +20 from one upvote. The votes map is a ConcurrentHashMap, and a teammate says "it is already thread-safe".

Languages: Java · Kotlin
Integer old = votes.put(voter, dir);          // ConcurrentHashMap
int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
score += delta;                               // int field
author.reputation += delta * upRep();         // int field
val old = votes.put(voter, dir)               // ConcurrentHashMap
val delta = dir - (old ?: 0)
score += delta                                // Int field
author.reputation += delta * upRep            // Int field
questions.promptHtml: Is it thread-safe? Explain the failure and give the fix.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Agrees that a concurrent map makes it safe, or adds a synchronized on the whole forum.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Single JVM or many app servers? Do votes also go to a DB? Can the same user vote on many posts in parallel (yes)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Make vote synchronized per post and recount scores of the posts affected.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) put itself is atomic, but put + score += + rep += is a compound action; (b) score += delta is read-modify-write, a lost update across different voters; (c) reputation is shared by all of an author's posts, so locking per post does not protect it.
  4. How I'd verify each: 2 threads x 100,000 same-voter votes: final score must be 1; 100 voters: score must equal the sum of ledger.
  5. Root cause: Individually atomic operations do not make a multi-step invariant atomic. put is atomic, but score += delta and reputation += ... are read-modify-write on plain ints, so concurrent updates are lost or doubled, and any code that does get then put lets two threads both see no old vote and both apply a full +1.
  6. Fix:
Languages: Java · Kotlin
synchronized void vote(User voter, int dir) {      // lock per post
    if (voter == author) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no self vote");
    Integer old = votes.put(voter, dir);
    int delta = dir - (old == null ? 0 : old);
    score += delta;
    author.addReputation(delta * (delta > 0 ? upRep() : upRep() / 2));   // AtomicInteger inside
}
@Synchronized fun vote(voter: User, dir: Int) {
    require(voter !== author) { "no self vote" }
    val delta = dir - (votes.put(voter, dir) ?: 0)
    score += delta
    author.addReputation(delta * if (delta > 0) upRep else upRep / 2)
}
  1. Prevention: Concurrent stress test; idempotent API (client sends vote id); DB constraint as the final guard.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: No global forum lock. No lock held across two posts, so no deadlock risk. Per-post lock serialises votes of one post only.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Many app servers? -> JVM locks do nothing; use SQL upsert with unique (post_id,user_id) and UPDATE ... SET score = score + :delta.
  • Why AtomicInteger for reputation? -> Different posts' locks do not exclude each other, but both update the same author.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A like counter on a ConcurrentHashMap passed review, then drifted by a few percent under load; a recount job exposed the lost updates.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: believes a concurrent map suffices.
  • Hire: per-post lock plus atomic reputation.
  • Strong hire: points out two lock scopes and the DB-level equivalent.

questions.contextHtml:
A viral question receives 4,000 votes/min. The SQL implementation is:

BEGIN;
INSERT INTO votes(post_id,user_id,value) VALUES (:p,:u,:v)
  ON CONFLICT (post_id,user_id) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value;
UPDATE posts SET score = (SELECT SUM(value) FROM votes WHERE post_id = :p) WHERE id = :p;
UPDATE users SET reputation = reputation + :d WHERE id = :author;
COMMIT;

Metrics: vote endpoint p99 from 30 ms to 6 s, DB shows 180 sessions waiting on transactionid locks, the SUM scans 900,000 vote rows per call. Red herring: CPU on the app tier is idle.
questions.promptHtml: What is happening and how do you fix it without losing correctness?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add an index" (one exists on post_id) or "scale the DB".

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is an exact live score required, or is a few seconds of lag fine? Same author for hot posts, so is the user row hot as well?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Stop recomputing SUM; apply score = score + :delta where delta is computed from the old value in the same statement; shorten transactions.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) every vote takes a row lock on the same posts row, so all votes serialise; (b) SUM over 900k rows inside the lock multiplies hold time; (c) the author's users row is a second hot row.
  4. How I'd verify each: pg_stat_activity wait events; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on the SUM; lock graph by pg_locks.
  5. Root cause: A hot-row update inside long transactions. One row can only be updated by one transaction at a time, so throughput is about 1 / lock hold time. At roughly 100 ms hold (the SUM over 900,000 rows) that is about 10 votes/s against the 67/s needed (4,000/min), so the queue of waiters grows without bound. With a 1 ms delta update the same row handles about 1,000/s.
  6. Fix: Short term: delta update, no SUM, SELECT old FOR UPDATE only on the vote row. Long term: buffer votes (Redis or a queue) and apply batched counter updates every second per post; keep the votes table as the ledger; periodic reconcile job; reputation updated asynchronously in batches.
  7. Prevention: Load test with a single hot post; alert on lock wait time and transaction duration; reconcile counter versus ledger nightly.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not move to eventual consistency for the votes ledger itself (a uniqueness guarantee), only for displayed counters. I would not remove the unique constraint.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Batched counter loses data on crash? -> Ledger is the truth; recount from it.
  • Isolation level? -> Read committed is enough with the unique key and atomic delta updates; serializable would just add retries.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "likes" counter on one celebrity post caused a global DB incident until counters were sharded into N sub-counters and summed on read.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: indexes or bigger DB.
  • Hire: delta update, no SUM, batching.
  • Strong hire: hot-row maths, sharded counters, ledger as truth, reconcile job.

questions.contextHtml:
In a code review you see:

Languages: Java · Kotlin
void accept(User asker, Answer a) {
    if (asker != author) throw new SecurityException("only asker accepts");
    if (accepted != null) { accepted.accepted = false; accepted.author.reputation -= 15; }
    accepted = a; a.accepted = true; a.author.reputation += 15;
}
fun accept(asker: User, a: Answer) {
    check(asker === author) { "only asker accepts" }
    accepted?.let { it.accepted = false; it.author.reputation -= 15 }
    accepted = a; a.accepted = true; a.author.reputation += 15
}

Defects reported over a month: an asker earned +15 by accepting their own answer, an answer from another question got accepted, and two threads accepting at once left two answers with accepted == true.
questions.promptHtml: List all the problems and rewrite the method.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Only adds the author check. Misses cross-question answers and the concurrency.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does accepting your own answer give rep (in Stack Overflow it does not)? Can the asker un-accept without choosing another? Is answers the authoritative list?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Repair data: for each question keep only the latest accepted answer and recompute reputations from the ledger.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) no check that a belongs to this question; (b) self-accept pays rep; (c) un-accept then re-accept the same answer pays 0 net but is noisy, and re-accepting the same answer when already accepted should be a no-op; (d) not atomic, two interleaved accepts break the single-accepted invariant.
  4. How I'd verify each: Unit tests for each defect; a two-thread test asserting at most one accepted answer.
  5. Root cause: The method trusts its inputs and modifies three objects without a critical section.
  6. Fix:
Languages: Java · Kotlin
synchronized void accept(User asker, Answer a) {
    if (asker != author) throw new SecurityException("only asker accepts");
    if (!answers.contains(a)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("answer not on this question");
    if (a == accepted) return;                                  // idempotent
    if (accepted != null) { accepted.accepted = false; revoke(accepted); }
    accepted = a; a.accepted = true; grant(a);                  // grant skips self-answers
}
private void grant(Answer a)  { if (a.author != author) a.author.addReputation(15); }
private void revoke(Answer a) { if (a.author != author) a.author.addReputation(-15); }
@Synchronized fun accept(asker: User, a: Answer) {
    check(asker === author) { "only asker accepts" }
    require(a in answers) { "answer not on this question" }
    if (a === accepted) return
    accepted?.let { it.accepted = false; revoke(it) }
    accepted = a; a.accepted = true; grant(a)
}
private fun grant(a: Answer) { if (a.author !== author) a.author.addReputation(15) }
private fun revoke(a: Answer) { if (a.author !== author) a.author.addReputation(-15) }
  1. Prevention: Make the single-accepted rule an invariant checked in tests; keep accepted only on Question and derive the answer's flag from it.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I would not duplicate the state (accepted on the question and on the answer); duplication is why they diverged. Derive isAccepted from the question.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Rep for the asker too? -> Stack Overflow gives the asker +2 in addition (verify current values); put both in the policy.
  • Deleting the accepted answer? -> Revoke on delete, through the same path.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: Two representations of the same fact (flag on answer and pointer on question) drifted for months; one data source removed a whole class of bugs.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: adds one check.
  • Hire: cross-question, self-accept, idempotency.
  • Strong hire: also single source of truth, atomicity, and revoke on delete.
